# Battle of Écija (1039)

The Battle of Écija (1039) was a battle that took place near the town of Écija in 3 October 1039, between the forces of the Taifa of Seville led by Ismail ibn Abbad and the allied forces of the Taifa of Málaga , Taifa of Granada and the Taifa of Carmona, the battle was a response to the Abbadid dynasty expansionist policies in the neighboring Taifas territories. The battle ended with a coalition victory and the death of Ismail ibn Abbad.
Background
In order to get the submission of the neighboring cities of Seville to the false Hisham II, Ismail ibn Muhammad ibn Abbad launched a campaign in which he defeated and executed Yahya ibn Ali ibn Hammud al-Mu'tali in 1036, some sources says that Yahya was preparing for a siege on Seville from Carmona and once he left the city to a lofty mountain for reconnoitering he was ambushed by the enemy and got killed, then ibn Abbad attacked his former ally Muhammad ibn Abdallah al-Birzali and seized Osuna and Écija, eventually besieging Carmona, Muhammad al-Birzali feared the Abbadid expansionist campaign and an anti-Abbadid coalition was formed with Badis ibn Habus king of the Taifa of Granada and Idris I al-Muta'ayyad king of the Taifa of Málaga.
Battle
the allies led by Badis ibn Habus and his vizier Samuel ibn Naghrillah, confronted Ismail ibn Abbad near the town of Écija, where the latter got defeated and killed, putting an end to his campaign in the region.
Aftermath
the towns of Osuna and Écija were likely re-captured by Muhammad ibn Abdallah al-Birzali who completed his reign in Carmona, until he was defeated and killed by Samuel ibn Naghrillah's Taifa of Granada forces, subsequently adding Écija to the realm of Badis ibn Habus kingdom in 1044.
